models.name: hrm_time_tracking_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts for unauthenticated visitors performing authentication operations.

Guests exist exclusively during the authentication lifecycle: signing up for new accounts, logging in to existing accounts, or accepting invitations to join organizations. Once authenticated, guests transition to members and operate within an organization context.

The email address must be unique across the entire platform, ensuring no duplicate accounts exist. Guests have no access to organization-specific data or features until they become authenticated members.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address for authentication. Must be unique across the entire platform. Used for both sign-up and login operations.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Required for account creation during sign-up and verification during login.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft-deleted. Null if the account is active.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access during signup, login, and invitation acceptance flows.

Each guest session tracks the connection context (IP address, current URL, referrer) and maintains temporal boundaries through creation and expiration timestamps. Sessions are created when an unauthenticated visitor interacts with authentication flows and expire after a defined period for security purposes.

Related to {@link hrm_time_tracking_guests} as the actor whose session is being tracked.

foreignFields.name: guest_id
foreignFields.description: The guest actor who owns this session. {@link hrm_time_tracking_guests.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client connection initiating the guest session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Current URL path where the guest session was initiated, useful for redirecting after authentication.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating where the guest came from before initiating the session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session expires. Sessions must have a defined expiration for security.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_members
models.description:
Registered user accounts representing individual persons who access the ERP platform.

Each member authenticates with a globally unique email address and password. Members can belong to multiple organizations simultaneously, with their global profile (display name, avatar, phone) shared across all organizations.

When logging in, members select an organization context, after which all actions are scoped to that organization. Members can switch between organizations without logging out.

Related entities:
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions} - Session tokens for authentication
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_member_password_resets} - Password recovery tokens
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees} - Organization memberships linking users to organizations

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address serving as the primary identifier for authentication. Must be unique across the entire platform; no two users can share the same email address.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. The password can be changed by the user at any time after logging in.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: The name shown to other users within organizations. This is how the user is identified in collaborative features such as task assignments, timesheet reviews, and team views. Shared across all organizations the user belongs to.

plainFields.name: avatar_image
plainFields.description: Optional URL to the user's profile picture that appears alongside their display name throughout the platform interface. Changes are immediately reflected across all organizations.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Optional contact number that can be shared with organization members.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created during initial sign-up.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last modified, including profile updates and password changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft-deleted. Null for active accounts. When set, the user can no longer authenticate.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_member_sessions
models.description: JWT session tokens for authenticated members tracking login sessions with connection metadata for security auditing. Each session belongs to a member and records IP address, current URL, referrer, creation timestamp, and expiration time. Organization context for multi-tenancy is managed at the application layer through the member's organization membership. Sessions are automatically invalidated when expired_at is reached.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The authenticated member this session belongs to. {@link hrm_time_tracking_members.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the member logged in, used for security auditing and session validation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL the member was accessing when the session was created, typically the login redirect target.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header from the login request, useful for tracking session origin and security analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created, marking the beginning of the authenticated session.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Always set to enforce session security and prevent indefinite sessions.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens with expiration for members who need to recover or change their password.

This table stores temporary, single-use tokens that allow members to securely reset their passwords. Each token has a limited validity period defined by the expires_at timestamp, after which it becomes invalid. Members can have multiple reset tokens (e.g., if they request multiple resets), but typically only the most recent valid token is used.

The table supports both password recovery (forgotten password) and password change workflows. Tokens are cryptographically random strings that should be included in password reset links sent via email.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The member account for which this password reset token was created. {@link hrm_time_tracking_members.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique, cryptographically random token string used to identify and validate the password reset request. This token should be included in the password reset link sent to the member's email address.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token expires. After this time, the token is no longer valid and cannot be used to reset the password. Typical expiration is 1-24 hours from creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was soft-deleted (used or invalidated). Nullable field for audit trail purposes.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_organizations
models.description: Multi-tenant organization entities that serve as the foundation for data isolation. Each organization owns all business data including employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets. Contains organizational settings: name, description, logo image, currency (USD/EUR/KRW), timezone, and fiscal start month. The owner reference links to the {@link hrm_time_tracking_members} who created the organization. Organization deletion cascades to all related data when constraints (no active contracts, all timesheets resolved) are met.

foreignFields.name: owner_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the organization owner. {@link hrm_time_tracking_members.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Organization display name used throughout the application for identification and display purposes.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description providing additional context about the organization's purpose, business focus, or other relevant information.

plainFields.name: logo_url
plainFields.description: URL to the organization's logo image file for branding and visual identification in the application.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Organization's base currency code for financial calculations. Supported values: USD (US Dollar), EUR (Euro), KRW (Korean Won).

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description: Organization's default timezone for date/time display and calculations. Standard IANA timezone identifier (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Asia/Seoul', 'Europe/London').

plainFields.name: fiscal_start_month
plainFields.description: Month number (1-12) when the organization's fiscal year begins. January = 1, December = 12. Used for reporting and budget calculations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was deleted (soft delete). Null if the organization is active.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_roles
models.description:
Role definitions within organizations governing employee permissions and access control.

Each organization maintains its own set of roles including three built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) that are created automatically and cannot be deleted. Organization owners can create custom roles with specific permission sets tailored to their operational needs.

Roles are assigned to employees within the organization, determining their capabilities for employee management, project management, time tracking, timesheet approval, and report access. Built-in roles have predefined permission sets, while custom roles can be configured with any combination of available permissions.

Related entities:
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations} - Organization that owns this role
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_members} - Member who created this role (for custom roles)
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions} - Permission assignments for this role
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees} - Employees assigned to this role

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization this role belongs to. Roles are organization-specific and isolated per tenant. {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: created_by
foreignFields.description: The member who created this role. Only populated for custom roles; built-in roles have this field as null since they are auto-generated. {@link hrm_time_tracking_members.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The name of the role. Built-in roles use 'Owner', 'Manager', and 'Employee'. Custom roles can have organization-specific names. Must be unique within the organization.

plainFields.name: is_built_in
plainFields.description: Whether this is a built-in role (Owner, Manager, Employee) that cannot be deleted. Built-in roles are created automatically when an organization is created and have predefined permission sets.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the role was created. For built-in roles, this matches the organization creation time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the role was last modified. Built-in roles may have limited update capabilities.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the role was soft-deleted. Built-in roles cannot be deleted. Custom roles can only be deleted when no employees are assigned.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions
models.description:
Permission assignments for roles within organizations, storing granular permission codes that define what actions employees with the assigned role can perform.

Each role can have multiple permissions from the available set including: org:manage (edit organization settings), employee:manage (add, edit, deactivate employees), employee:view (view employee list and details), project:manage (create, edit, delete projects and tasks), project:view (view projects and tasks), time:manage (edit or delete any employee's timelogs), time:approve (approve or reject timesheets), time:view_all (view all employees' timelogs and timesheets), and report:view (view organization reports).

Permission changes take effect immediately for all employees assigned to the role. Built-in roles have predefined permission sets that cannot be modified, while custom roles allow flexible permission assignment by organization owners.

Related entities:
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_roles} - The role to which this permission is assigned
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations} - Organization that owns the role (via role FK)

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_tracking_role_id
foreignFields.description: The role to which this permission is assigned. {@link hrm_time_tracking_roles.id}

plainFields.name: permission
plainFields.description: The permission code assigned to the role. Valid values include: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view. Each permission grants specific capabilities within the organization.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the permission was assigned to the role. Used for audit trail to track when permissions were granted.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_employees
models.description:
Employee records linking authenticated users to organizations with role assignment, optional department membership, position title, employment type classification, and activation status.

Each employee represents a user's membership in a specific organization with an assigned role that determines their permissions. An employee belongs to exactly one organization and has exactly one role within that organization at any given time. Employees may optionally be assigned to a department for organizational grouping.

The employment type field categorizes the worker relationship (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern) for reporting and payroll purposes. The status field tracks whether the employee is active and can log time, or deactivated with preserved historical data.

Users with employee management permission can create, edit, and deactivate employee records. Employees can view their own profile and other employees in their organization based on their role permissions. All employee data is strictly isolated by organization boundary.

Key relationships:
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_members} - The user account this employee record belongs to
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations} - The organization this employee works in
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_roles} - The role assigned to this employee determining permissions
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_departments} - Optional department this employee belongs to

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The user account this employee record belongs to. Each user can have one employee record per organization. {@link hrm_time_tracking_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization this employee belongs to. All employee data is scoped to this organization. {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations.id}.

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description: The role assigned to this employee, determining their permissions within the organization. Each employee has exactly one role at any given time. {@link hrm_time_tracking_roles.id}.

foreignFields.name: department_id
foreignFields.description: Optional department this employee belongs to for organizational grouping. Department membership is optional and can be changed. {@link hrm_time_tracking_departments.id}.

plainFields.name: position
plainFields.description: Job position or title for this employee within the organization, such as 'Software Engineer' or 'Project Manager'. Optional field that can be updated by users with employee management permission.

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description: Employment type classification for payroll and reporting purposes. Valid values: 'full-time', 'part-time', 'contractor', 'intern'. This field is required and determines how the employee's time and compensation are tracked.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the employee record. Valid values: 'active', 'deactivated'. Active employees can log time and submit timesheets. Deactivated employees cannot log time but their historical data is preserved. Can be reactivated by users with employee management permission.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the employee record was created. Set automatically when an employee is added to the organization.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the employee record was last modified. Updated automatically when any field is changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the employee was soft-deleted. Null if the employee is active or deactivated. Soft delete preserves historical timelog and timesheet data for auditing purposes.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_employee_invitations
models.description:
Pending invitations for new employees sent by email before account creation.

When a user with employee management permission invites someone by email, this table tracks the invitation if the email has no existing account. The invitation stores the assigned role and optional department that will be applied when the invited user signs up. Once the user creates an account with the invited email, they are automatically added to the organization with the specified role, and the invitation status transitions to 'accepted'.

Related entities:
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations} - Organization the invitation belongs to
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_roles} - Role to assign when employee is created
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_departments} - Optional department assignment
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_members} - Member who sent the invitation

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization to which the invited employee will belong. {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations.id}.

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description: The role that will be assigned to the employee when they accept the invitation. {@link hrm_time_tracking_roles.id}.

foreignFields.name: department_id
foreignFields.description: Optional department that will be assigned to the employee upon joining. {@link hrm_time_tracking_departments.id}.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who sent the invitation. {@link hrm_time_tracking_members.id}.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address of the invited person. When they sign up with this email, the invitation will be automatically accepted.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the invitation: 'pending' (awaiting signup), 'accepted' (user has signed up and joined), 'expired' (invitation no longer valid).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was created and sent.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was soft deleted. Null if not deleted.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_contracts
models.description:
Employment contracts tracking pay rate, pay period, working hours, and duration for each employee.

Each contract represents the formal employment terms between an organization and an employee for a defined period. Contracts serve as historical records of compensation agreements and expected work commitments. An employee can have multiple contracts over time, but only one contract can be active at any given time.

Past contracts (those with end_date in the past) are immutable historical records and cannot be modified. Only the current active contract can be edited by users with appropriate permissions.

Relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees} (required)
- Supports historical employment tracking through start_date and end_date fields

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_tracking_employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee who holds this contract. Each contract belongs to exactly one employee. {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees.id}

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: The date when the employment terms take effect. Required field indicating when the contract period begins.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: The date when the employment terms expire. When not specified (null), the contract represents an ongoing employment arrangement with no predetermined conclusion. When specified, it marks when the employment terms end.

plainFields.name: pay_rate
plainFields.description: The numeric compensation amount as specified in the contract. The actual meaning (hourly rate, daily rate, etc.) is determined by the pay_period field.

plainFields.name: pay_period
plainFields.description: How frequently compensation is calculated and paid. Allowed values: 'hourly' (compensation calculated per hour worked), 'daily' (compensation calculated per day worked), 'weekly' (compensation calculated per week), 'monthly' (compensation calculated per month).

plainFields.name: working_hours_per_week
plainFields.description: The expected working hours per week as specified in the contract. Establishes the standard time commitment for the employee (e.g., 40 hours).

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional additional information about the employment terms, special conditions, or other relevant details.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the contract record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the contract record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the contract was soft-deleted. Null if the contract is active.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_departments
models.description:
Organizational departments within multi-tenant organizations that group employees by functional area.

Each department belongs to exactly one organization and supports one level of nesting through an optional parent department reference. This allows for hierarchical department structures like Engineering > Backend Team.

Departments are managed by users with org:manage permission. When a department is deleted, employees assigned to that department have their department reference cleared (set to null) but are not deleted themselves.

Related entities: {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees} can optionally belong to a department.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization this department belongs to. Departments are strictly isolated per organization. {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: parent_department_id
foreignFields.description: Optional parent department for one-level nesting hierarchy. Enables structures like 'Engineering > Backend Team'. Null for top-level departments. {@link hrm_time_tracking_departments.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Department name, unique within the organization. Examples: 'Engineering', 'Marketing', 'Human Resources'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description of the department's purpose and responsibilities.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was soft-deleted. Null if the department is active.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_projects
models.description:
Projects representing distinct bodies of work or initiatives within an organization, serving as containers for tasks and time tracking.

Each project has a name, optional description, color code for visual identification, status tracking through active/archived/completed lifecycle, optional budget hours for estimation, and optional date range for scheduling. Projects belong to organizations and serve as the primary organizational unit for task management and time tracking.

Projects can be archived or completed to prevent new timelogs while preserving historical data. Project deletion is only allowed when no timelogs are associated. Projects have members assigned through {@link hrm_time_tracking_project_members} and tasks created within them through {@link hrm_time_tracking_tasks}.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_tracking_organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization this project belongs to. {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Project name, unique within the organization. Used for identification and display purposes.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description of the project's purpose, scope, and objectives.

plainFields.name: color_code
plainFields.description: Hexadecimal color code for UI display and visual identification (e.g., '#FF5733'). Required for visual differentiation in project lists and reports.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Project status indicating current lifecycle state. Valid values: 'active' (ongoing work), 'archived' (temporarily suspended), 'completed' (finished). Archived and completed projects cannot receive new timelogs.

plainFields.name: budget_hours
plainFields.description: Total estimated hours for the project budget. Used for tracking budget utilization in reports. Optional - projects without budget are excluded from budget reports.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Project start date for scheduling and timeline tracking. Optional field for project planning.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description: Project end date for scheduling and timeline tracking. Optional field for project planning and deadline management.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was soft-deleted. Null if project is active. Soft delete preserves historical timelog data.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_project_members
models.description:
Project memberships linking employees to projects with assigned roles, enabling role-based task management permissions within projects.

Each membership represents an employee's participation in a project with a specific role that determines their access level. Project leads can manage tasks within their assigned project, while members have standard project participation access.

The unique constraint on employee and project prevents duplicate membership assignments. Employees can be members of multiple projects simultaneously, and each project can have multiple members with varying roles.

Related entities: {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees} (the employee assigned to the project), {@link hrm_time_tracking_projects} (the project the employee is assigned to).

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee assigned to the project. Must be an active employee within the same organization as the project. {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees.id}.

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: The project the employee is assigned to. Determines the project context for the membership role. {@link hrm_time_tracking_projects.id}.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description: The assigned role within the project. Either 'member' for standard project participation access, or 'project_lead' for task management permissions within the project.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was removed (soft delete). Null if the membership is active.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_tasks
models.description:
Work items within projects representing specific units of work that can be tracked, assigned, and monitored.

Each task has a required title describing the work to be performed and an optional description providing additional context. Tasks support planning through optional estimated hours for effort planning and due date for deadline tracking.

Tasks progress through four status values: open (awaiting work), in-progress (being worked on), completed (finished), and closed (no longer active). Priority levels (low, medium, high, urgent) indicate task urgency for work prioritization.

Tasks support single-level nesting through parent task relationships, enabling hierarchical organization of work as subtasks. A subtask cannot itself have subtasks. Tasks can be assigned to employees who are members of the containing project.

All task status changes are recorded in {@link hrm_time_tracking_task_histories} for audit trail purposes. Time spent on tasks is tracked through {@link hrm_time_tracking_timelogs}.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_tracking_project_id
foreignFields.description: The project this task belongs to. Tasks are always associated with a specific project. {@link hrm_time_tracking_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_tracking_employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee assigned to this task, who must be a member of the containing project. Optional assignment for workload distribution and accountability. {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: parent_task_id
foreignFields.description: The parent task for subtask relationships. Only one level of nesting is supported - a subtask cannot have its own subtasks. Null for top-level tasks. {@link hrm_time_tracking_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The title of the task, concisely describing the work to be performed.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description providing additional context, instructions, or details about the work to be performed.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The current status of the task. Valid values: 'open' (newly created awaiting work), 'in-progress' (currently being worked on), 'completed' (finished), 'closed' (no longer active).

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: The urgency level of the task for work prioritization. Valid values: 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'urgent'.

plainFields.name: estimated_hours
plainFields.description: The anticipated time required to complete the task, in hours. Used for effort planning and progress tracking.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: The deadline by which the task should be completed. Used for deadline tracking and prioritization.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the task was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the task was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the task was soft-deleted. Null if the task is still active.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_task_histories
models.description:
Audit trail capturing task modifications within projects, recording each field change with timestamp, previous value, new value, and the member who performed the change.

This table serves as an immutable historical record of task lifecycle transitions including status changes, priority updates, assignment modifications, and field edits. Each entry represents a single field modification on a task, providing complete traceability for compliance and debugging purposes.

The history entries are append-only and cannot be modified or deleted once created, ensuring audit integrity. Entries are linked to the task being modified and the member who performed the action.

foreignFields.name: task_id
foreignFields.description: The task that was modified. {@link hrm_time_tracking_tasks.id}.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who performed the modification. {@link hrm_time_tracking_members.id}.

plainFields.name: field_name
plainFields.description: The name of the task field that was modified (e.g., 'status', 'priority', 'title', 'assigned_employee_id', 'due_date').

plainFields.name: previous_value
plainFields.description: The value of the field before the modification. Null when a field is being set for the first time.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: The value of the field after the modification. Null when a field is being cleared or unset.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the modification was recorded. Captures the exact moment of the change for audit trail purposes.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_timelogs
models.description:
Individual time entries recording work performed by employees on specific dates.

Each timelog captures the date of work, duration in minutes, and optional description of work performed. Timelogs must be associated with a project the employee is assigned to, and optionally with a specific task within that project.

The billable flag indicates whether the time should be considered for billing purposes (defaults to true). Employees can designate time as non-billable for internal work.

Timelogs can be included in timesheets for approval. Once part of an approved timesheet, timelogs become locked and cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring integrity of approved time records.

Relationships:
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees} - The employee who logged the time
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_projects} - The project the time was logged against
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_tasks} - Optional task the time was logged against
- {@link hrm_time_tracking_timesheets} - Optional timesheet containing this timelog (when submitted)

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee who logged this time entry. Employees can only create timelogs for themselves. {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: The project this time was logged against. The employee must be a project member to log time on this project. {@link hrm_time_tracking_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: task_id
foreignFields.description: Optional task this time was logged against. When specified, the task must belong to the same project. {@link hrm_time_tracking_tasks.id}

foreignFields.name: timesheet_id
foreignFields.description: Optional timesheet this timelog belongs to. Set when the timelog is included in a submitted timesheet. When the timesheet is approved, this timelog becomes locked. {@link hrm_time_tracking_timesheets.id}

plainFields.name: date
plainFields.description: The date when the work was performed. Used for timesheet week grouping and date-range filtering.

plainFields.name: duration_minutes
plainFields.description: Duration of work in minutes. Provides granular time tracking for billing and reporting purposes.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description of what work was performed. Provides context for the time entry.

plainFields.name: billable
plainFields.description: Whether this time should be considered for billing purposes. Defaults to true. Set to false for internal or non-billable work.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timelog was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timelog was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timelog was soft-deleted. Preserved for historical records and recovery.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_timesheets
models.description:
Weekly timesheet collections aggregating employee timelogs from Monday to Sunday for approval workflow management.

Each timesheet represents a complete work week for an employee, serving as the submission unit for time tracking approval. Timesheets progress through a defined workflow: draft (editable) → submitted (awaiting approval) → approved (finalized, locks timelogs) or rejected (returns to draft with reason).

Timesheets enforce one-per-employee-per-week constraints and aggregate total hours from included timelogs. Approved timesheets lock all associated timelogs, preventing further modifications to ensure data integrity for payroll and reporting purposes.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees} as the timesheet owner
- Reviewed by {@link hrm_time_tracking_members} when approved or rejected
- Contains multiple {@link hrm_time_tracking_timelogs} entries within the week date range

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_tracking_employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee who owns this timesheet. References {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees.id}. Each employee can have one timesheet per week.

foreignFields.name: reviewer_id
foreignFields.description: The member who reviewed (approved or rejected) this timesheet. References {@link hrm_time_tracking_members.id}. Populated when timesheet transitions from submitted to approved or rejected status.

plainFields.name: week_start_date
plainFields.description: The start date of the timesheet week, always a Monday. Defines the beginning of the seven-day period covered by this timesheet.

plainFields.name: week_end_date
plainFields.description: The end date of the timesheet week, always a Sunday. Defines the end of the seven-day period covered by this timesheet.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The current status of the timesheet in the approval workflow. Valid values: 'draft' (editable), 'submitted' (awaiting approval), 'approved' (finalized), 'rejected' (returned to draft with reason). Transitions: draft→submitted→approved, or submitted→rejected→draft.

plainFields.name: total_hours
plainFields.description: The total hours calculated from all included timelogs. Automatically recalculated when timelogs are added or removed from the timesheet.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the timesheet was submitted for approval. Populated when status transitions from draft to submitted.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the timesheet was reviewed (approved or rejected). Populated when status transitions from submitted to approved or rejected.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided when rejecting a timesheet. Required when a reviewer rejects a submitted timesheet. Visible to the employee for correction guidance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the timesheet was created. Automatically set upon creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the timesheet was last modified. Automatically updated on any change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the timesheet was soft-deleted. Null for active timesheets. Enables data recovery and audit trail preservation.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_timers
models.description:
Real-time tracking sessions for employees that record work in progress.

Each timer represents an active time tracking session that an employee has started. The timer captures the start timestamp, the project being worked on, an optional specific task, and an optional description of the work being performed. When an employee stops the timer, the elapsed duration (rounded to nearest minute) is used to create a timelog entry. Alternatively, employees may discard timers to cancel tracking without creating any timelog record.

Employees can have at most one active timer at any time. This constraint is enforced at the application layer. Timers continue running indefinitely until the employee manually intervenes - there is no automatic stop mechanism. Employees can edit the project, task, and description of a running timer.

Soft delete is supported via deleted_at field to maintain audit trail and align with data retention policies.

Relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees} (the employee tracking time)
- References {@link hrm_time_tracking_projects} (required - where work is performed)
- Optionally references {@link hrm_time_tracking_tasks} (specific task if applicable)

foreignFields.name: employee_id
foreignFields.description: The employee who owns this timer session. {@link hrm_time_tracking_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: The project this timer is tracking time against. Required as time must be associated with a project. {@link hrm_time_tracking_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: task_id
foreignFields.description: The optional specific task being worked on during this timer session. {@link hrm_time_tracking_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description of the work being performed during this timer session. Can be edited while the timer is running.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timer was started. This is the start time used for calculating duration when the timer is stopped.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timer was last modified (e.g., description or project/task changed).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timer was discarded or soft-deleted. When null, the timer is active or was stopped (converted to timelog). When set, the timer was discarded without creating a timelog.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs
models.description:
Main audit trail entries recording all significant organizational actions including employee management, project lifecycle, contract changes, task status changes, timesheet events, and role assignments. Each entry captures the timestamp, the member who performed the action, the action type, optional target entity reference, organization context, and optional details.

Action types include: employee_invited, employee_deactivated, employee_reactivated, contract_created, contract_edited, project_created, project_archived, project_completed, project_deleted, task_status_changed, timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, timesheet_rejected, role_assigned, role_changed.

Users with org:manage permission can view and filter the activity log by action type, user, and date range. Activity log entries are permanent audit records and cannot be modified or deleted.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: The member who performed the action. {@link hrm_time_tracking_members.id}

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization context for this activity. Enforces multi-tenant data isolation. {@link hrm_time_tracking_organizations.id}

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: The type of action performed. Allowed values: employee_invited, employee_deactivated, employee_reactivated, contract_created, contract_edited, project_created, project_archived, project_completed, project_deleted, task_status_changed, timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, timesheet_rejected, role_assigned, role_changed.

plainFields.name: target_entity_type
plainFields.description: The type of entity that was affected by the action. Examples: employee, contract, project, task, timesheet, role. Used with target_entity_id for polymorphic entity reference.

plainFields.name: target_entity_id
plainFields.description: The UUID of the entity that was affected by the action. Combined with target_entity_type to form a polymorphic reference to any entity in the system.

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Optional JSON-encoded details about the action. For task_status_changed: includes old_status and new_status. For role_assigned/role_changed: includes role name. For timesheet_rejected: includes rejection reason. NOTE: This field is deprecated in favor of normalized child tables (activity_log_task_status_details, activity_log_role_change_details, activity_log_timesheet_rejection_details).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the activity was recorded. Activity logs are append-only and immutable.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_snapshots
models.description:
Entity state snapshots captured at the time of activity log creation, storing contextual data such as previous/new values for role changes, entity names, and other action-specific metadata for enhanced audit trail detail.

Each snapshot represents a single field change within an activity log entry. When multiple properties of an entity change simultaneously (e.g., a task status change from 'open' to 'in-progress'), each field change is recorded as a separate snapshot record linked to the same parent activity log.

This design supports the comprehensive audit requirements for actions including: employee lifecycle events (invited, deactivated, reactivated), contract modifications, project lifecycle transitions (created, archived, completed, deleted), task status progression, timesheet workflow decisions (submitted, approved, rejected), and role assignment changes.

The entity_name field captures the human-readable name of the target entity at the moment of the action, preserving historical context even if the underlying entity is subsequently renamed or deleted.

As a subsidiary entity of {@link hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs}, this table is not directly exposed through user-facing APIs. Snapshots are created automatically during activity log creation and remain immutable for the lifetime of the audit record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_id
foreignFields.description: The parent activity log entry this snapshot belongs to. References {@link hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs.id}.

plainFields.name: field_name
plainFields.description: The name of the field that changed (e.g., 'status', 'role', 'employment_type', 'pay_rate'). Used to identify what aspect of the entity was modified in this snapshot.

plainFields.name: previous_value
plainFields.description: The value before the change. Nullable for creation events where no previous value exists (e.g., 'Employee invited' has no prior state). Stored as string for flexibility across different field types.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: The value after the change. Nullable for deletion events where no subsequent value exists. Stored as string for flexibility across different field types.

plainFields.name: entity_name
plainFields.description: Display name of the target entity at the time of the action (e.g., employee name, project name, task title). Captured for historical reference even if the entity is later renamed or deleted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Aligns with the parent activity log timestamp for consistent audit trail ordering.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_task_status_details
models.description:
Normalized detail records for task_status_changed activity log entries, storing the previous and new task status values as separate atomic fields for First Normal Form (1NF) compliance.

Each record provides the specific status transition data for task status change events in the audit trail. The previous_status field is nullable to accommodate initial task creation events where no prior status existed. This table maintains a one-to-one relationship with {@link hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs} - each task status change activity log has exactly one corresponding detail record with the transition specifics.

Task status values follow the project management workflow: open (awaiting work), in-progress (being worked on), completed (finished), and closed (no longer active). These detail records are immutable and serve as the authoritative source for understanding task lifecycle transitions in the organization's audit trail.

foreignFields.name: activity_log_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent activity log entry. Each task status change activity log has exactly one detail record. {@link hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs.id}.

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description: The task status before this change. Nullable for initial task creation events where no previous status exists. Valid values: open, in-progress, completed, closed.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: The task status after this change. Always has a value since every status change produces a new current status. Valid values: open, in-progress, completed, closed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this detail record was created, coinciding with the task status change event.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_role_change_details
models.description:
Normalized detail records for role_assigned and role_changed activity log entries, storing the new role name and previous role name as separate atomic fields for First Normal Form (1NF) compliance.

Each record has a one-to-one relationship with a parent activity log entry of type 'role_assigned' or 'role_changed'. For initial role assignments, the previous_role_name field is null. For role changes, both fields contain values to support before/after comparisons in audit reports.

This normalization pattern avoids storing structured data in a generic 'details' field and enables efficient querying of role change history.

foreignFields.name: activity_log_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent activity log entry. {@link hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs.id}

plainFields.name: role_name
plainFields.description: The name of the newly assigned role at the time of the activity log entry.

plainFields.name: previous_role_name
plainFields.description: The name of the previously assigned role before this change. Null for initial role assignments when the employee had no prior role.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this detail record was created, synchronized with the parent activity log entry.

models.name: hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_timesheet_rejection_details
models.description:
Normalized details for timesheet_rejected activity logs, storing the rejection reason as an atomic field for 1NF compliance.

This subsidiary table maintains a 1:1 relationship with activity_logs entries where the action type is 'timesheet_rejected'. When a manager rejects a submitted timesheet, the rejection reason is captured here to explain why the timesheet was not approved. This separation ensures clean data normalization and allows the main activity_logs table to remain general-purpose while still capturing all necessary contextual information.

The rejection reason supports the timesheet rejection workflow by providing employees with actionable feedback to modify and resubmit their timesheets.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_tracking_activity_log_id
foreignFields.description: The activity log entry for timesheet rejection. Each activity log has at most one timesheet rejection detail record. {@link hrm_time_tracking_activity_logs.id}

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided when a timesheet was rejected, explaining why the submission was not approved. This feedback helps employees understand what needs to be corrected before resubmission.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timesheet rejection detail record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timesheet rejection detail record was last updated.
